previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis and a history of hepatic encephalopathy was admitted with altered mental status, worsening abdominal and back pain, and signs of infection including fever, tachycardia, and hypotension. She had recently been treated for C. difficile infection and was no longer taking lubiprostone. Initial labs showed leukocytosis and mild transaminitis, but imaging revealed no acute abdominal process, ascites, or source of infection. Blood cultures remained negative, and the C. difficile test was cancelled due to formed stool. She was treated with IV fluids and ceftriaxone for presumed sepsis, with improvement in mental status on lactulose for hepatic encephalopathy. Antibiotics were transitioned to oral levofloxacin for completion at home. Her pain was attributed to chronic IBS and a stable T10 paraspinal mass. She was discharged home with stable vital signs, improved cognition, and a plan to start linaclotide after insurance approval, with close follow-up arranged.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ is a ___ year-old right-handed woman with history 
of EtOH cirrhosis (CHILDS B, MELD 12) c/b varices, 
encephalopathy, ascites pending transplant, recently admitted 
___ to ___ Medicine for GI sepsis/encephalopathy, who 
presented with a constellation of subacute neurological symptoms 
including R facial droop, right arm/leg weakness and R face 
numbness. 

# Neurological Symptoms: On admission exam, there was mild R 
nasolabial fold flattening at rest, but upon activation of her 
facial musculature she exhibited a symmetric smile. Per the 
inpatient stroke team, she initially exhibited an upper motor 
neuron pattern of weakness in the RUE/RLE, though the exam of 
the RLE was limited by pain. She also had a right V1-V3 sensory 
loss to pin prick, 75% compared to the left, which did not split 
midline. There was also decreased sensation in the RLE>RUE. 
Given constellation of symptoms, she was admitted to the stroke 
service for workup. EKG showed normal sinus rhythm. CT showed no 
evidence of acute infarction, hemorrhage, edema, or mass effect. 
MRI/MRA brain was also unremarkable. In addition, her 
neurological symptoms changed over time - her right nasolabial 
fold flattening was not always present, and at times she 
exhibited left nasolabial fold flattening, but always exhibited 
a symmetric smile with activation of facial muscles. The 
neurology team felt that her symptoms were not able to be 
explained by a neurological disorder and transferred the patient 
to the medicine service for management of the patient's mild 
encephalopathy.

# Encephalopathy: The patient had been discharged from the 
medicine service on ___ after an admission for encephalopathy 
thought secondary to SBP (although formal diagnosis was not made 
due to lack of ascites to tap). Per her sister, the patient was 
less encephalopathic at time of transfer to the medicine service 
than she had been at time of last discharge. She was treated 
with Q2H lactulose before decreasing this to Q4H on ___. Her 
encephalopathy improved with this treatment. Urine culture and 
blood cultures were unremarkable with the exception of 1 bottle 
growing GPCs in chains consistent with contamination. She 
remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable. The patient's LFTs 
were normal on admission and day 2 of her hospital stay. On 
hospital day 3, her AST/ALT/ALP increased from 38/24/124 to 
___. TBili, however remained wnl. The following day her 
AST/ALT/ALP downtrended to ___. Abdominal ultrasound with 
doppler revealed no ascites and normal flow in the portal 
vasculature. Having ruled out these causes of elevated LFTs and 
encephalopathy and with the patient's continued improving 
clinical status, she was able to be discharged with close PCP 
follow up within 3 days of discharge. She will have LFTs, coags, 
Chem-7 and CBC rechecked at that appointment.

==== TRANSITIONAL ISSUES ====

# Encephalopathy and Elevated LFTs
- PCP follow up on ___
- Please recheck CBC, Chem-7, LFTs and coags on ___
- Increased lactulose to QID

# Opioid and Benzodiazepine Use
- Strongly recommend against prescribing opioids or 
benzodiazepines as they can precipitate encephalopathy
- Tylenol (up to 2g per day) and, if needed, tramadol are more 
preferable choices

# Ongoing Proton Pump Inhibitor Use
- Please revisit patient's indication for omeprazole (currently 
on high dose 40mg BID). PPI use is associated with increased 
risk of SBP, C.difficile, and other high-risk infections in 
cirrhotic patients. Their use should be reserved for those 
patients with clear indications.
